title: Finite Q3 source-boundary quadratic Duhamel norm envelope and cutoff stress
question: Does source-boundary commutation give a finite quadratic-time action bound, and do the resulting norm constants remain controlled when the path volume and oscillator cutoff are varied?

model.real_time_action: alpha_t^H(A)=exp(i t H/hbar) A exp(-i t H/hbar)
model.derivation: The bound follows from the finite Duhamel identity, source commutation, automorphism isometry and ||[X,Y]||<=2||X||||Y||.
model.stress: The envelope is evaluated for oscillator dimensions 2 and 3 and nested path pairs; any growth is a cutoff/volume diagnostic, not a no-go theorem.

exact_interface.lean: R343 proves commutator(h0+delta,a)-commutator(h0,a)=commutator(delta,a) and its zero form under source-boundary commutation.
exact_interface.finite_bound: The operator-norm envelope is a conditional finite-matrix consequence of source commutation and the declared Duhamel action convention.

exact_interface.uniformity: The bound is not called source-, volume-, cutoff- or beta-uniform; its exact H0 and Delta norms are reported for every finite row.

adversarial_review.check: All action defects and bounds use the induced operator norm; no Frobenius norm is substituted for the stated envelope.
The exact Delta/source commutator is checked before the quadratic envelope is applied; a small numerical residual is not silently treated as an exact zero.
The coefficient is the conservative 2||Delta||( ||H0||+||Delta|| )||A||/hbar^2 obtained from Duhamel and two commutator norm inequalities; it is not fitted to the observed defects.
The min with 2||A|| uses unitary action isometry and is retained only as a second finite bound, not as a decay statement.
Higher-than-minimal first nonzero commutator orders are recorded as cancellations, while only the graph-distance lower bound is enforced.
Oscillator dimensions 2 and 3 are separate finite fixtures; their norm growth is evidence about this truncation family, not an unbounded-operator theorem.
Only path2, path3 and path4 are tested, and exact finite H0/Delta norms are reported; no volume-uniform extrapolation is made.
The independent lane rebuilds oscillator matrices, Q3 terms, nested embeddings, actions and norm envelopes without importing the primary lane.
R343 certifies only the finite associative commutator decomposition; the norm inequality and all numerical values remain finite Python evidence.

A finite norm envelope with cutoff/volume dependence does not prove a common OS carrier, uniform D/delta-D Cauchy, common alpha, Hamiltonian-OS identification, GNS gap, continuum, C6, Sector A or Pre-A.
